    theorem LargeIndecomposable.exists_zeroDetectingNormalizedLift_of_no_long_critical {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [HasBGRSPairDichotomy C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [∀ (X : C), IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [∀ (X : C), IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] [IsFiniteRayCategory (BGRSRayCategory C)] (hlong : ∀ {i j : RayVertex (BGRSRayCategory C)} (p : Quiver.Path i j), IsCriticalBGRSLiftSingularPath p → ¬3 ≤ p.length) (hdisjoint : ∀ (p q : SingularPairNormalization.SingularPair), (↑p).firstArrow = (↑q).firstArrow ∨ (↑p).firstArrow = (↑q).secondArrow ∨ (↑p).secondArrow = (↑q).firstArrow ∨ (↑p).secondArrow = (↑q).secondArrow → p = q) :
    ∃ (L : BGRSRayArrowLift), ∀ {i j : RayVertex (BGRSRayCategory C)} (p : Quiver.Path i j), L.pathMap p = 0 ↔ rayPathMap p = 0

    The two remaining source inputs—exclusion of long critical singular paths and disjointness of singular pairs—produce a global representative choice detecting exactly the zero ray paths. Distinctness of the two arrows inside a pair is derived from distributivity.
